A 52-year-old man with tall stature, pectus deformity, and a family history of sudden death develops abrupt chest pain while lifting a heavy box. The pain reaches maximal intensity immediately and radiates between the scapulae. Blood pressure is 178/92 mm Hg in the right arm and 142/78 mm Hg in the left. A new early diastolic murmur is present. CT angiography demonstrates a flap beginning in the ascending aorta and extending into the arch; the right renal artery intermittently fills from a compressed true lumen.

Which mechanism best explains the episodic reduction in right renal perfusion?

A 71-year-old woman with decompensated heart failure receives intravenous loop diuretics for 3 days. Her dyspnea improves, but a moderate unilateral pleural effusion persists. Pleural fluid protein is 3.3 g/dL, serum protein is 6.0 g/dL, pleural LDH is 150 U/L, and serum LDH is 230 U/L. The serum-to-pleural albumin gradient is 1.4 g/dL. Cultures and cytology are negative.

Why can this hydrostatic effusion satisfy exudative Light criteria after treatment?

A 46-year-old man is admitted with septic shock from an obstructed urinary tract. Two days later, he develops severe hypoxemia, bilateral air-space opacities, and a PaO2/FIO2 ratio of 92 despite positive-pressure ventilation. Echocardiography shows normal left ventricular systolic function. A pressure-volume curve demonstrates markedly reduced lung compliance. An illustrated lung section shows eosinophilic material lining collapsed alveoli.

Which primary pathophysiologic change produced these findings?

A 24-year-old cyclist falls onto an outstretched hand. He has focal tenderness in the anatomic snuffbox, but initial radiographs show no fracture. The wrist is immobilized. Repeat imaging 12 days later shows a nondisplaced fracture through the waist of the scaphoid. A diagram highlights arterial entry along the distal portion of the bone.

Which complication is the proximal fragment at greatest risk of developing?

A 39-year-old woman has recurrent urinary infections and now presents with fever, flank discomfort, and cloudy urine. Urinalysis shows a pH of 8.6 and rectangular coffin-lid crystals. CT demonstrates a branching calculus occupying the renal pelvis and calyces. Urine culture grows a motile gram-negative rod that produces urease.

Which biochemical change most directly promotes formation of this calculus?

A 10-year-old boy develops rapidly increasing abdominal girth and early satiety over 3 weeks. Imaging shows a large ileocecal mass. Serum lactate dehydrogenase and uric acid are markedly elevated. Biopsy demonstrates a monomorphic population of medium-sized B cells with numerous interspersed tingible-body macrophages, producing a starry-sky appearance. Ki-67 staining approaches 100%.

Which genomic event most likely drives this tumor's extreme proliferative rate?

A 31-year-old woman presents with gingival bleeding, fatigue, and widespread bruising. Platelets are 24,000/mm3, fibrinogen is low, and D-dimer is markedly elevated. A smear shows abnormal promyelocytes containing bundles of Auer rods. Cytogenetic analysis identifies t(15;17). Treatment is started immediately while supportive blood products are given.

How does the disease-specific therapy reverse the leukemic block?

A 66-year-old man has progressive edema, orthostatic lightheadedness, numb feet, and exertional dyspnea. Urine protein excretion is 5.8 g/day. Echocardiography shows thick ventricular walls with low-voltage electrocardiographic complexes. Serum immunofixation identifies a monoclonal lambda light chain. Abdominal fat-pad biopsy contains Congo-red-positive material with apple-green birefringence.

Which protein is the principal precursor of the deposited fibrils?

A 34-year-old aid worker returns from West Africa and develops fever, confusion, jaundice, and oliguria. Thin blood smear shows delicate ring forms, sometimes more than one in a single erythrocyte, and crescent-shaped gametocytes. Parasitemia is 8%. Brain imaging shows no focal lesion. The patient is treated urgently for severe malaria.

Which parasite property most directly contributes to his neurologic dysfunction?

A 58-year-old woman has episodic flushing, watery diarrhea, wheezing, and a new systolic murmur that increases with inspiration. CT shows a small ileal neuroendocrine tumor and multiple liver lesions. Urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid is elevated. Review of older imaging shows that the intestinal tumor was present for years before systemic symptoms appeared.

Why did the syndrome most likely become clinically apparent only after liver involvement developed?

A 43-year-old man with hypertension develops intermittent flank discomfort and gross hematuria after minor exercise. Imaging shows bilaterally enlarged kidneys containing numerous cysts and several hepatic cysts. His mother required dialysis at age 61, and his older sister survived rupture of an intracranial aneurysm.

Which additional lesion is this patient at increased risk of harboring?

A 37-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of pounding headache, palpitations, diaphoresis, and tremulousness. During one episode her blood pressure is 228/116 mm Hg. Plasma free metanephrines are elevated, and MRI reveals a 3-cm adrenal medullary mass. Surgery is planned after medical preparation.

Which medication sequence is most appropriate before tumor removal?

A 41-year-old man with untreated HIV infection presents with headache, fever, confusion, and left-arm weakness. His CD4 count is 38/mm3. MRI shows several ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia with surrounding edema. Toxoplasma IgG is positive. He improves after pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, and leucovorin.

Which process most likely produced these brain lesions?

A 45-year-old woman develops constant right upper-quadrant pain, fever, and nausea several hours after a fatty meal. Examination shows inspiratory arrest during deep palpation below the right costal margin. Ultrasound demonstrates a stone lodged at the gallbladder neck, wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, and a sonographic Murphy sign. The common bile duct is not dilated.

Which event most directly initiates this inflammatory process?

A 19-year-old man of Mediterranean ancestry is evaluated for chronic fatigue. Hemoglobin is 10.8 g/dL, MCV is 64 fL, ferritin is normal, and the erythrocyte count is relatively high for the hemoglobin level. The smear shows target cells and basophilic stippling. Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows increased HbA2 and mildly increased HbF.

Which cellular abnormality is chiefly responsible for his anemia?

A previously normotensive 29-year-old primigravida at 31 weeks has blood pressure readings of 166/104 and 162/102 mm Hg, new proteinuria, headache, and elevated liver transaminases. Doppler assessment earlier in pregnancy showed high-resistance uterine arterial flow. Laboratory testing demonstrates increased soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1.

Which placental abnormality initiated the maternal syndrome?

A 28-year-old laboratory technician reports progressive fatigue, recurrent mouth ulcers, and easy bruising. CBC shows pancytopenia with a very low reticulocyte count. There is no lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly. Bone-marrow biopsy is markedly hypocellular and largely replaced by fat; no malignant infiltrate or fibrosis is seen.

Which mechanism most commonly underlies acquired idiopathic disease of this type?

A 27-year-old man presents with a solitary painless penile ulcer and rubbery, nontender inguinal lymph nodes. Dark-field examination of ulcer fluid reveals thin motile spirochetes. The lesion resolves without treatment, but serologic testing is positive.

Which histopathologic process is most characteristic of this lesion?

A 26-year-old woman is evaluated after a soft systolic ejection murmur is noted at the left upper sternal border. She has normal oxygen saturation and no cyanosis. The second heart sound is widely split and changes little with respiration. Echocardiography shows a secundum atrial septal defect with left-to-right flow and right ventricular enlargement.

Why is the splitting of the second heart sound relatively fixed?

A 48-year-old man with infective endocarditis develops a new high-pitched early diastolic murmur along the left sternal border. His pulse is bounding, and blood pressure is 158/48 mm Hg. Echocardiography shows severe aortic regurgitation and acute left ventricular volume overload. A pressure-volume loop is constructed.

Which change is most characteristic of the loop in this patient?

A 3-year-old boy with a harsh systolic murmur becomes deeply cyanotic and tachypneic while crying. He instinctively squats and improves within minutes. Echocardiography shows a ventricular septal defect, an overriding aorta, right ventricular hypertrophy, and severe infundibular pulmonary stenosis.

How does squatting improve this episode?

A 42-year-old woman who emigrated from a region with limited access to antibiotics has progressive exertional dyspnea and occasional palpitations. Auscultation reveals a loud S1, an opening snap, and a low-pitched diastolic rumble at the apex. Echocardiography shows thickened commissurally fused mitral leaflets and marked left atrial enlargement.

Which hemodynamic abnormality is most directly responsible for her pulmonary symptoms?

A 30-year-old woman has chronic bloating, loose stools, iron deficiency, and an intensely pruritic vesicular eruption on the extensor surfaces of her elbows. Duodenal biopsy demonstrates villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes. Symptoms improve after eliminating wheat, barley, and rye.

Which molecular event is central to the intestinal immune response?

A 19-year-old college student develops tremor, personality change, and jaundice. Slit-lamp examination reveals brown rings at the corneal periphery. Serum ceruloplasmin is low, and 24-hour urinary copper excretion is elevated. Liver biopsy shows increased copper.

Which transport defect causes this disorder?

A 46-year-old woman has 8 months of symmetric pain and swelling in the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. Morning stiffness lasts 2 hours. Examination shows boggy synovitis, and radiographs reveal periarticular osteopenia and marginal erosions. Synovial biopsy demonstrates proliferative granulation tissue extending over articular cartilage.

Which process most directly produces the marginal bone erosions?

A 25-year-old woman has photosensitive facial erythema, oral ulcers, inflammatory hand pain, and edema. Urinalysis shows protein and red-cell casts. Antinuclear and anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies are positive, and serum C3 and C4 are low. Kidney biopsy shows granular capillary-wall and mesangial immunofluorescence.

Which immune mechanism best explains the renal lesion?

A 28-year-old woman has painful loss of vision in one eye that improves over several weeks. Eight months later she develops diplopia; examination shows impaired adduction of the left eye with nystagmus of the abducting right eye. MRI reveals periventricular ovoid lesions, and cerebrospinal fluid contains oligoclonal IgG bands.

Which cellular target is primarily damaged in this disorder?

A 20-year-old man has sudden episodes of rapid regular palpitations. Between episodes, ECG shows a short PR interval, a slurred initial upstroke of the QRS complex, and a mildly widened QRS. An electrophysiology diagram shows a muscular connection between atrium and ventricle outside the atrioventricular node.

Which property of this connection creates the baseline ECG pattern?

A 15-year-old boy awakens with sudden severe left scrotal pain and vomiting. The left testis is high-riding and horizontally oriented, and the cremasteric reflex is absent. Doppler ultrasonography shows markedly reduced intratesticular flow. Emergency exploration confirms twisting of the spermatic cord.

Which pathologic sequence occurs first after torsion?

A 54-year-old woman has nephrolithiasis, constipation, and diffuse bone discomfort. Calcium is 11.7 mg/dL, phosphate is low, and parathyroid hormone is elevated. Hand radiographs show subperiosteal bone resorption. Bone biopsy demonstrates increased osteoclast activity.

How does excess parathyroid hormone stimulate the osteoclasts?

A 38-year-old woman has progressive proximal weakness, easy bruising, wide violaceous abdominal striae, and new diabetes. Blood pressure is 172/98 mm Hg and potassium is low. Testing confirms marked cortisol excess from an adrenal cortical tumor with suppressed ACTH.

Which mechanism contributes most directly to her hypertension and hypokalemia?

A 24-year-old man develops hemoptysis, fatigue, and rapidly rising creatinine after a respiratory infection. Urinalysis shows dysmorphic red cells and red-cell casts. Kidney biopsy demonstrates crescent formation, and immunofluorescence shows smooth linear IgG staining along glomerular capillary loops.

Which antigen is targeted by the pathogenic antibody?

A 47-year-old man has recurrent sinus pain, bloody nasal discharge, cough with hemoptysis, and hematuria. CT shows cavitary pulmonary nodules. Creatinine is elevated, and urinalysis reveals red-cell casts. Proteinase-3 ANCA is strongly positive. Kidney immunofluorescence shows little or no immune deposition.

Which histologic finding is most characteristic outside the kidney?

A 6-year-old boy has recurrent episodes of painless maroon-colored stool. He is afebrile and has no abdominal tenderness. Hemoglobin is low. A technetium-99m pertechnetate scan shows a focus of uptake in the right lower abdomen that appears at the same time as the stomach.

Which process most directly causes the intestinal bleeding?

A 33-year-old man develops tingling in his feet followed by symmetric ascending weakness 10 days after a diarrheal illness. Deep-tendon reflexes are absent. Cerebrospinal fluid has elevated protein with only 2 leukocytes/mm3. Nerve-conduction studies show slowed velocity and conduction block.

Which mechanism most likely initiated this neurologic disorder?

An 8-year-old boy is evaluated for intellectual disability, social anxiety, hand flapping, and poor eye contact. Examination shows a long narrow face, prominent ears, and enlarged testes. His maternal uncle has similar cognitive impairment. Molecular testing demonstrates a large CGG expansion in the 5-prime untranslated region of a gene on the X chromosome.

How does the full mutation reduce gene expression?

A 14-year-old girl collapses while swimming and spontaneously regains consciousness. Her mother has had unexplained syncope, and a maternal cousin died suddenly at age 18. ECG shows a corrected QT interval of 520 ms. Genetic testing identifies a loss-of-function variant in KCNQ1.

Which action-potential change results from this mutation?

A 7-year-old girl has seizures, developmental delay, hypopigmented ash-leaf macules, facial angiofibromas, and a shagreen patch. Brain MRI shows cortical tubers, and renal imaging shows bilateral angiomyolipomas. Genetic testing reveals loss of function in TSC2.

Which signaling abnormality promotes these lesions?

A 50-year-old man has years of migratory arthralgias followed by weight loss, diarrhea, and abdominal distention. Small-bowel biopsy shows villi expanded by foamy macrophages containing periodic acid-Schiff-positive, acid-fast-negative material. Electron microscopy reveals bacillary structures within macrophages.

Which organism is the most likely cause?

An 11-year-old boy develops fever, migratory pain and swelling of large joints, a new apical holosystolic murmur, and purposeless movements 3 weeks after an untreated sore throat. Antistreptolysin O and anti-DNase B titers are elevated. Blood cultures are negative.

Which immune process best explains this syndrome?
